rationale: All three reverse (alpha>1) the repetition-specific write direction of mid-depth Gated-DeltaNet out_proj columns, derived from the atlas as W*mean(Δ input) over branch rep-vs-prod and natural loop-vs-preloop, restricted to the top-k columns by rep contribution. #1 is a single rank-1 edit on L12 linear_attn (k=320, a=10): branch_rep -2.03 with the best side-effect margins (prod -0.007, close -0.23, neutral +0.008); the k=256 variant held up on held-out branch cases (fit -2.04 vs held-out -1.86), its projection rises in 18/18 natural loop traces, and a random-u control on the same columns scores 0. #2 adds L14 amplification (a=-8), which works only because the L12 reversal already flips L14's component. It is stronger on branch_rep (-2.28) and within limits (prod -0.010, neutral -0.004), but it depends on that interplay, and on its own L14 amplification costs neutral -0.025, so it carries more risk in real generation. #3 is a different lever, the L14 reversal with an L15 MLP neutral compensator (branch_rep -2.21, prod -0.011, close -0.02, neutral -0.009). Of the three, its direction is the best grounded in natural loops: a natural-only direction keeps about 47% of the effect, and held-out cases score -1.66 vs fit -1.74. It sits close to the neutral limit.
